[id="{anchor_prefix}-github-com-kubewarden-gateway-protector-api-v1alpha1-policytargetreference"]
==== PolicyTargetReference



PolicyTargetReference identifies the Gateway API object (Gateway or
HTTPRoute) that a WAFPolicy/DLPPolicy attaches to.

It mirrors the upstream Gateway API policy-attachment reference form (see
sigs.k8s.io/gateway-api/apis/v1.NamespacedPolicyTargetReference), extended
with an optional SectionName so a policy can target a single listener
(when Kind is Gateway) or a single route rule (when Kind is HTTPRoute).
Upstream does not currently ship a combined Namespace+SectionName
reference type, so this struct is hand-written rather than reused
directly.



.Appears In:
****
- xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-kubewarden-gateway-protector-api-v1alpha1-wafpolicyspec[$$WAFPolicySpec$$]
****

[cols="20a,50a,15a,15a", options="header"]
|===
| Field | Description | Default | Validation
| *`group`* __link:https://gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io/reference/api-spec/main/spec/#group[$$Group$$]__ | group is the group of the target resource. + |  | Required: \{} +

| *`kind`* __link:https://gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io/reference/api-spec/main/spec/#kind[$$Kind$$]__ | kind is the kind of the target resource. Only "Gateway" and "HTTPRoute" +
(group gateway.networking.k8s.io) are supported. + |  | Enum: [Gateway HTTPRoute] +
Required: \{} +

| *`name`* __link:https://gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io/reference/api-spec/main/spec/#objectname[$$ObjectName$$]__ | name is the name of the target resource. + |  | Required: \{} +

| *`namespace`* __link:https://gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io/reference/api-spec/main/spec/#namespace[$$Namespace$$]__ | namespace is the namespace of the target resource. WAFPolicy/DLPPolicy +
objects live in the platform-owned namespace (e.g. +
gateway-protector-system) while the targeted Gateway/HTTPRoute usually +
lives elsewhere, so this field is required to let the controller +
resolve cross-namespace targets unambiguously. + |  | Required: \{} +

| *`sectionName`* __link:https://gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io/reference/api-spec/main/spec/#sectionname[$$SectionName$$]__ | sectionName targets a specific listener (when kind is Gateway) or a +
specific route rule (when kind is HTTPRoute). When unset, the policy +
applies to the whole Gateway/HTTPRoute. + |  | Optional: \{} +

|===

[id="{anchor_prefix}-github-com-kubewarden-gateway-protector-api-v1alpha1-wafcustomrule"]
==== WAFCustomRule



WAFCustomRule is a single raw Coraza/ModSecurity SecRule directive block,
identified by its numeric rule id.



.Appears In:
****
- xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-kubewarden-gateway-protector-api-v1alpha1-wafrulesetspec[$$WAFRuleSetSpec$$]
****

[cols="20a,50a,15a,15a", options="header"]
|===
| Field | Description | Default | Validation
| *`id`* __integer__ | id is the numeric SecRule id. It must be in the site-local range +
1-99999, which is the SecLang convention reserved for a site's own +
custom rules (as opposed to 100000-899999, historically assigned to +
various commercial/community rule vendors; 900000-999999, the OWASP +
Core Rule Set itself; 9500000-9599999, registered CRS plugins; and +
10000000-10000099, reserved by gateway-protector for its own +
generated directives). It is +
the author's responsibility to keep ids unique within a WAFRuleSet +
and across every other WAFRuleSet referenced by the same WAFPolicy. +

This validates the declared id field only, not any id that might +
also appear inside the raw directive text below - a mismatch between +
the two is still only caught at dry-compile time. + |  | Required: \{} +

| *`directive`* __string__ | directive is one or more raw SecRule lines composing this rule. + |  | MinLength: 1 +
Required: \{} +

|===

[id="{anchor_prefix}-github-com-kubewarden-gateway-protector-api-v1alpha1-wafenginespec"]
==== WAFEngineSpec



WAFEngineSpec configures the WAF engine's operating mode.

There is deliberately no failure-posture (fail-open/fail-closed) knob
here: the data plane this project integrates with (agentgateway's
ext_proc wiring) hardcodes fail-closed when the processor is
unreachable and exposes no way to configure it, so this API doesn't
promise a behavior it cannot deliver. If upstream ever exposes it, a
failureMode field can be reintroduced.



.Appears In:
****
- xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-kubewarden-gateway-protector-api-v1alpha1-wafpolicyspec[$$WAFPolicySpec$$]
****

[cols="20a,50a,15a,15a", options="header"]
|===
| Field | Description | Default | Validation
| *`mode`* __xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-kubewarden-gateway-protector-api-v1alpha1-wafenginemode[$$WAFEngineMode$$]__ | mode selects whether the engine blocks, only logs, or is disabled. + |  | Enum: [Blocking Detection Off] +
Required: \{} +

|===

[id="{anchor_prefix}-github-com-kubewarden-gateway-protector-api-v1alpha1-wafpolicyspec"]
==== WAFPolicySpec



WAFPolicySpec defines the desired state of WAFPolicy.

A WAFPolicy attaches a Coraza + OWASP Core Rule Set WAF engine to a
Gateway (as the default for all its routes) or to a single HTTPRoute (as
an override of the Gateway default for that route only) - resolved
"most-specific-wins" between exactly those two attachment levels, with no
merging: a Route-level WAFPolicy fully replaces the Gateway-level one for
that route, it doesn't add to it. See the field docs below for the
per-field reference, docs/wafpolicy-lifecycle.md for the validation and
conflict-resolution rules, and docs/processor.md for how the compiled
result is ultimately consumed by the data plane.



.Appears In:
****
- xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-kubewarden-gateway-protector-api-v1alpha1-wafpolicy[$$WAFPolicy$$]
****

[cols="20a,50a,15a,15a", options="header"]
|===
| Field | Description | Default | Validation
| *`targetRef`* __xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-kubewarden-gateway-protector-api-v1alpha1-policytargetreference[$$PolicyTargetReference$$]__ | targetRef identifies exactly one Gateway (applies to all its routes, +
the common default case) or one HTTPRoute (overrides the Gateway +
default for that route only). + |  | Required: \{} +

| *`engine`* __xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-kubewarden-gateway-protector-api-v1alpha1-wafenginespec[$$WAFEngineSpec$$]__ | engine configures the WAF engine's mode and failure posture. + |  | Required: \{} +

| *`paranoiaLevel`* __integer__ | paranoiaLevel selects the CRS paranoia level (1-4); higher levels +
enable more (and more false-positive-prone) rules. Absent means the +
Core Rule Set's own default (paranoia level 1). + |  | Maximum: 4 +
Minimum: 1 +
Optional: \{} +

| *`anomalyThreshold`* __xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-kubewarden-gateway-protector-api-v1alpha1-wafanomalythreshold[$$WAFAnomalyThreshold$$]__ | anomalyThreshold sets the inbound/outbound anomaly score thresholds. +
Absent means the Core Rule Set's own defaults. + |  | Optional: \{} +

| *`requestBody`* __xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-kubewarden-gateway-protector-api-v1alpha1-wafbodyinspectionspec[$$WAFBodyInspectionSpec$$]__ | requestBody configures request body inspection. + |  | Optional: \{} +

| *`responseBody`* __xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-kubewarden-gateway-protector-api-v1alpha1-wafbodyinspectionspec[$$WAFBodyInspectionSpec$$]__ | responseBody configures response body inspection. + |  | Optional: \{} +

| *`exclusions`* __xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-kubewarden-gateway-protector-api-v1alpha1-wafexclusion[$$WAFExclusion$$] array__ | exclusions silence specific CRS rules (by id or tag), e.g. to resolve a +
known false positive without lowering the paranoia level. + |  | Optional: \{} +

| *`customRulesRefs`* __xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-kubewarden-gateway-protector-api-v1alpha1-localrulesetreference[$$LocalRuleSetReference$$] array__ | customRulesRefs references WAFRuleSet objects, in the same namespace as +
this WAFPolicy, whose custom SecRule directives are compiled into the +
engine alongside the Core Rule Set. Referenced WAFRuleSets are +
rendered in namespace/name order, not the order listed here (this is +
a listType=map, so list order isn't meaningful and isn't preserved +
across a server-side-apply merge); SecLang rules that depend on a +
specific relative order must be placed together within a single +
WAFRuleSet, whose own spec.rules order is preserved. + |  | Optional: \{} +

|===
